newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto seen opening stronger after tumble.
newsitem.headline: Toronto seen opening stronger after tumble.

text.p: Toronto stocks were expected to open stronger on Tuesday and recoup some of yesterday's losses after overnight bargain-hunting of U.S. securities and an early European recovery soothed investors' jitters.
"They have about half of the loss back already in European trading, so I think we're going to see an up morning, or at least an upstart, and from there we may drift lower again," one trader said.
North American stocks plunged yesterday after remarks by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto created fears about a possible Japanese disposal of U.S. treasuries.
The trader said the sell-off was a timely demonstration of the volatility of North America's towering markets, "where one comment by one person can create the downdraft that it did."

"I think what was said, whether it was misinterpreted or not, has always been an option...but it just goes to show you how edgy people are when you've got the indexes up at these levels. If this had happened at 5000 it probably wouldn't have made much difference," he said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index dropped 73.72 points or 1.1 percent to close at 6437.71.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell nearly 2.5 percent or 192 points to 7604, the second-greatest point plunge after Black Monday's 508-point crash on October 19, 1987.

Golds were expected to remain under pressure on Tuesday, offset by stong banks after several of Canada's major banks cut long-term mortgage rates on Monday, taking the cost of five-year loans to 7.0 percent from 7.15 percent.
"That should probably help the banks but it won't do much for gold," the trader said.
In economic news, the number of Canadians who applied for employment insurance benefits in April rose 0.4 percent in April from March, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
The agency said claims rose to 229,000 in April from 228,000 in March according to seasonally adjusted data.
Canadian department stores sales rose a seasonally adjusted 1.2 percent in May from April to C$1.31 billion, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
In unadjusted data, year-over-year sales in May rose 11.6 percent to C$1.29 billion.
* Minority shareholders of Southam Inc yesterday voted to reject the C$923 million bid by Conrad Black's Hollinger Inc to take the newspaper chain private.

* Corel Corp said after market close on Monday it made a slim operating profit of US$4.1 million in its second quarter, but a US$113.7 million writedown of capitalized software assets pushed the company into the red in the quarter. After the charge, Corel lost US$1.49 compared to a profit of US$0.01 in the same period last year.
